episodes.title: MALADAPTIVE INTERPERSONAL OPERATING SYSTEMS
episodes.description:
If a conversation with someone follows you home — you're still hearing their words hours later, still rehearsing your reply days later — you may not be dealing with a mood. You may be dealing with a system.

In this video, Dr. Peter Salerno breaks down the four maladaptive interpersonal operating systems behind predatory behavior — the framework at the heart of his book, The Social Predator's Secret Playbook. You'll learn how to tell a bad season from a dangerous pattern, and the one distinction that changes everything: characteristic, not symptomatic.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN

Why you never need to diagnose anyone to recognize a dangerous pattern.

The four operating systems: 
Impulsive–Aggressive 
Entitled–Exploitative
Callous–Exploitative,
Attention–Extorting

Why apologies in these systems restore access — not behavior

Covert vs. overt deployment, and why the switch between them is a choice, not a slip

The single pattern to watch for: enduring harm, void of accountability


GET THE BOOK
The Social Predator's Secret Playbook: Traits and Tactics of Pathological Personalities — and How to Recognize Them

Also by Dr. Salerno: Cruelty by Nature · Traumatic Cognitive Dissonance · The Nature and Nurture of Narcissism · What If I'm Wrong?!? (You're Not)

All descriptions are of behavior patterns — this content does not label, diagnose, or classify any individual. episodes.title: USING BALANCE THEORY TO REDUCE TRAUMATIC COGNITIVE DISSONANCE
episodes.description:
When you're trying to make sense of a relationship that's left you confused, your mind is quietly juggling three separate things at once — and it tends to blur them together. The first is how you regard your partner: your overall feeling toward them, from deeply loving to deeply hurt. The second is how you regard their actions: whether the specific things they do actually help you or cost you. And the third is the story you tell yourself about why they act that way — whether it's something in their control, or something you've decided to excuse.

The trouble is, when those three get tangled, a warm feeling about the person can quietly rewrite how you judge what they did. The Triangle Tool pulls them back apart so you can look at each one honestly, on its own.

In this video, Dr. Lieberman and I walk through the Triangle Tool together — where it comes from in the science, how the three corners connect, and how to actually use it on a real moment from your own relationship.
